name: Variables
what: A named place to store a value.
why: Programs need to remember data like names and scores.
real: A labelled jar in a kitchen: you can change what's inside.
mistake: Using a variable before giving it a value.
exercise: Create variables for your name and your age, then print them.

name: Functions
what: A reusable block of code that does one job.
why: They avoid repeating code and keep programs tidy.
example:
function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
add(2, 3);
real: A recipe: same steps each time, with different ingredients.
mistake: Forgetting to return a value or to call the function.
exercise: Write a function that returns the square of a number.

name: Classes
what: A blueprint for creating objects.
why: They group data and behavior together.
real: A house plan used to build many houses.
mistake: Forgetting new when creating an object.
exercise: Create a Car class with a brand and a start() method.

name: Objects
what: A thing that holds related data and actions.
why: They model real things like users or products.
real: A student card with name, number and course.
mistake: Reading a property that doesn't exist (undefined).
exercise: Make an object for your favorite book with title and author.

name: Arrays
what: An ordered list of values.
why: They store many items under one name.
real: A shopping list where each line has a number, starting at 0.
mistake: Off-by-one mistakes: the last index is length - 1.
exercise: Make an array of 3 names and print the second.

name: Loops
what: Code that repeats until a condition is met.
why: They save you from writing the same thing many times.
real: Washing dishes until the pile is empty.
mistake: An endless loop because the condition never becomes false.
exercise: Print the numbers 1 to 10 with a loop.

name: Conditions
what: Code that chooses what to run depending on a true/false test.
why: Programs must react to different situations.
real: If it rains, take an umbrella; otherwise, don't.
mistake: Using = (assign) instead of == or === (compare).
exercise: Print 'pass' if a mark is 50 or more, otherwise 'fail'.

name: APIs
what: A way for programs to talk to each other by requests.
why: They let your app use data and features from other services.
real: A waiter carrying your order to the kitchen and bringing food back.
mistake: Not handling errors or slow responses.
exercise: Describe what request a weather app would make.

name: Databases
what: Organized storage for data that persists.
why: Apps need to keep data after they close.
example: SELECT name FROM students WHERE grade > 60;
real: A big filing cabinet with labelled drawers.
mistake: Forgetting WHERE in UPDATE or DELETE.
exercise: Design a table for books: which columns would you use?

name: Git
what: A tool that tracks changes to your code over time.
why: You can undo mistakes and work with others.
example:
git add .
git commit -m "feat: add login"
git push
real: Save points in a video game.
mistake: Committing without a clear message, or committing secrets.
exercise: Create a repo, make a commit, and view git log.

name: REST APIs
what: An API style that uses URLs and HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).
why: It gives a standard, predictable way to build web services.
real: A menu: each item name (URL) plus an action (method).
mistake: Using GET to change data.
exercise: List the 4 methods for a 'products' resource.

name: MVC
what: Model-View-Controller: splits an app into data, display and logic.
why: It keeps code organized and easier to change.
example:
Model: User
View: profile page
Controller: handles the request
real: A restaurant: pantry (model), dining room (view), waiter (controller).
mistake: Putting database logic inside the view.
exercise: Name the M, V and C in a to-do app.

name: OOP
what: Object-Oriented Programming: building software from objects with data and behavior.
why: It helps reuse code and model real things.
example:
class Animal { speak() {} }
class Cat extends Animal { speak() { return 'meow'; } }
real: Vehicles share basics, but a car and a bike differ.
mistake: Making inheritance chains too deep.
exercise: Create Animal and Dog classes where Dog extends Animal.

name: Exception handling
what: Catching errors so the program doesn't crash.
why: Users get a friendly message instead of a crash.
real: A safety net under a trapeze.
mistake: Catching an error and ignoring it silently.
exercise: Wrap a division by zero check in a try/catch.

name: React Components
what: A reusable piece of UI written as a function that returns JSX.
why: They break a page into small pieces you can reuse.
real: Lego bricks: the same brick can be used many times.
mistake: Naming a component in lowercase (it must start with a capital).
exercise: Make a Button component that takes a label prop.

name: Hooks
what: Special React functions like useState and useEffect for state and side effects.
why: They let function components remember data and react to changes.
real: A notebook the component keeps between renders.
mistake: Calling hooks inside conditions or loops.
exercise: Build a counter with useState.

name: Async/Await
what: A readable way to wait for slow tasks like network requests.
why: It makes asynchronous code read like normal steps.
example:
const res = await fetch(url);
const data = await res.json();
real: Waiting for your coffee order before sitting down.
mistake: Forgetting await, or await outside an async function.
exercise: Fetch a URL with async/await and log the result.

name: Promises
what: An object that represents a future result (success or failure).
why: They handle tasks that finish later.
real: A restaurant buzzer: it will ring when the food is ready or the order fails.
mistake: Not adding .catch for errors.
exercise: Wrap a setTimeout in a Promise.

name: JSON
what: A text format for storing and sending data.
why: Programs and APIs share data in the same simple format.
real: A standard shipping label everyone can read.
mistake: Trailing commas or single quotes (not allowed).
exercise: Write JSON for a book with title and author.

name: Recursion
what: A function that calls itself to solve smaller versions of a problem.
why: It's a natural fit for trees, folders and repeated patterns.
real: Russian nesting dolls: open one to find a smaller one.
mistake: Forgetting the base case, causing endless calls.
exercise: Write a recursive function to sum 1 to n.
